newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.N. protests against detention of Bosnian Serb.
newsitem.headline: U.N. protests against detention of Bosnian Serb.

text.p: United Nations and human rights observers protested to Moslem-Croat authorities on Monday over what they said was the unlawful detention in northern Bosnia of a Bosnian Serb war-crimes suspect.

The U.N. International Police Task Force said in a statement that Milorad Marceta, 52, who faced war crimes charges in a court in Bihac on Friday, had been detained despite the fact that prosecutors had failed to produce any evidence against him.

U.N. human rights lawyers, present at the hearing, accused the Moslem-Croat justice authorities of irregularities, saying that Marceta had not been allowed to see his lawyer before the hearing, the statement said.
The Task Force said it was "continuing to protest the detention of Milorad Marceta."

Marceta was detained by the Bosnian police in Sanski Most on Tuesday as he crossed over the border from the Bosnian Serb controlled part of the country to visit his former home now under Moslem-Croat administration.
His arrest contravened the Rome Agreement of February 18 agreement governing the detention of war-crimes suspects, the Task Force statement said.

Despite U.N. requests, Moslem-Croat investigators have failed to submit Marceta's files to the U.N. International War Crimes Tribunal, which has not listed the Bosnian Serb as a war criminal, the statement said.
Under the Dayton accord which ended the 43-month war last November, refugees have the right to cross inter-ethnic boundary lines and visit their homes.
But this has not been implemented by nationalist rulers who want their adminstrative boundaries to become firm borders around their ethnically pure states.
